4. How Do I Research My Niche?
Before you choose a niche for your YouTube channel, it is important to do a thorough demand,  competition & longevity analysis. Researching audience demand and preferences helps you tailor your content to meet their needs and interests.
A thorough research of the competition helps you identify gaps and opportunities while selecting the best niche for YouTube. By understanding your niche and the competition, you can develop a strategy to stand out and make your content unique. It will also help you understand the monetizing potential of your niche which can help you generate more income. 
There are several methods you can use to research demand and competition while choosing the best niche for YouTube. 
4.1. Conduct Keyword Research
Use keyword research tools such as Google Keyword Planner, the YouTube search bar, Google Trends, and VidIQ to identify popular search terms associated with your niche. See if they have high search volumes and consistent interest. It can help you understand your niche or interest’s potential value. 
You can use the following methods to conduct keyword research 
Youtube search method/Alphabet soup
To do keyword and topic research for a niche via the YouTube search bar, follow these steps:

Type a broad keyword related to your niche in the YouTube search bar
Look at the suggested search terms that appear below the search bar, as this can give you an idea of what people are searching for related to your niche



Scroll through the search results and look at the titles and descriptions of the top videos to see what topics are popular in your niche
Look at the number of views, likes, and comments on the top videos to gauge the level of interest in those topics
Use the "Filter" option on the search results page to narrow down the results by upload date, view count, and other criteria to find more specific topics and trends in your niche

Google Trends Method 
Google Trends is a tool that can be used to analyze the popularity of search terms over time. To use Google Trends for keyword and topic research for YouTube, follow these steps:

Visit Google Trends 
Enter a broad keyword related to your niche in the search bar



Use the filters below your keyword at the top of the page to narrow down the results by location, time period, and category (e.g., Arts & Entertainment, Sports, etc.)



Look at the "Interest over time" graph to see how the popularity of the keyword has changed over time



Scroll down to the "Related queries" section to see other search terms that are related to your keyword



Click on a related query to see its "Interest over time" graph and related queries
Repeat the process for each related query to find new topics and search terms to explore

VidIQ 
VidIQ can help you find relevant and high-ranking keywords associated with videos. To do a keyword research on VidIQ, follow these steps: 

Start by installing the VidIQ browser extension for Chrome or Firefox. You can find the extension on the respective web stores and add it to your browser
Go to YouTube and you will see the VidIQ extension icon in your browser at the top right. Click the drop down icon to open the menu
In the VidIQ panel, click on the Keyword Inspector option. Here, you'll find various keyword suggestions related to the video's topic 



In Keyword Inspector, type in your broad keyword and hit search to get your results. VidIQ assigns scores to each keyword, indicating its potential value. Pay attention to the Search volume, Competition, and Overall score to assess the keyword's viability.


You can do this much by accessing VidIQ’s free extension. VidIQ Pro offers more features but you might not need it for basic keyword research. 
Google keyword planner
Google Keyword Planner can help you gain valuable insights into the search volume and competition level for keywords related to your niche. Follow these steps to use it:   

Go to the Google Keyword Planner website and log in with your Google account
Click on "Discover new keywords" and enter a broad keyword related to your niche
Specify your targeting options, such as location and language
Click "Get results" to generate a list of keywords related to your niche
Sort the list by relevance, search volume, or other criteria to find the most relevant keywords for your niche
Click on a keyword to see additional data, such as search volume trends and competition level
Use the keyword data to inform your content strategy, including video titles, tags, and descriptions.

4.2. Analyze Competition
Apart from keyword research, you also need to analyze the competition for your niche on YouTube. Visit the channels of your top competitors and examine their statistics such as subscriber count, total video views as well as engagement metrics such as likes, comments and shares. 
Analyzing the comments section of your competition’s videos can help you get insights into audience preference and content gaps. For instance, check out these comments on Marques Brownlee’s iPhone 14 review on YouTube. You get a fair idea that the content he is sharing is informative and appreciated by his audience. 

Make sure you watch several videos as well to understand your competition’s content strategy. Take a look at the videos they produce, their format and the topics they cover. You can then gauge what works and what doesn’t.
Going through your competitions videos will also help you understand if they have collaborated with other creators, companies or brands and how well affiliate marketing or brand sponsorships work for them.
Based on your analysis, you can identify gaps and opportunities which can help you plan your strategy and create meaningful content. 
4.3. Use Social Media
You can use social media to analyze a niche for YouTube to gain valuable insights into audience interest, engagement and trends. Identify key platforms which are relevant for your niche. 
While Facebook, Instagram, Twitter and TikTok are popular platforms to start with, you might want to check out the other platforms where your audience spends its time. For instance, if your niche is talking about everything NFT, then you might want to check out platforms such as Telegram, Discord and Reddit. 
Social media platforms are also a great way to keep an eye on trending topics within your niche and help you get insights into current interests and popular discussions. 
4.4. Survey Your Audience
Once you have a small following, you can survey your audience to understand their preferences and interests. This can help you tailor your content to their needs and preferences and build a loyal following.
Apart from encouraging your audience to leave suggestions, opinions or feedback in the comments section and engaging with them there, here are a few other ways in which you can survey your audience:

Community Tab: If your channel is eligible, you can use the Community Tab feature to post polls and questions directly to your subscribers
Video Poll Cards: During your videos, use YouTube's interactive poll cards. These are on-screen annotations that allow viewers to vote on a specific question while watching your video
Video End Screens: Use end screens to prompt viewers to take a survey or participate in a poll related to the video they just watched

4.5. Real World Research

For instance, Cassey Ho, the founder of Blogilates started her channel by creating online pilates videos for her students. As she was moving away from her hometown, she didn’t want her students to miss out and at the time, roughly around 2009, there was a gap in the market for an online pilates instructor. Since then, her POP Pilates videos have garnered over millions of views.
If you already have real-world proof that your content or services are needed, you can start from there itself. Filling in gaps with valuable and relevant content allows you to position your channel uniquely and attract a dedicated audience seeking the specific information or service you provide.
4.6. Longevity Test
If you have zeroed in on a niche, it’s important to check its longevity too. Is it just a passing trend or is it evergreen? Here are several things you can do to verify the longevity of a niche.

Historical Consistency: Use tools like Google Trends, YouTube's own search tools, or specialized SEO tools to analyze the historical search volume and interest for topics in your niche. If there is consistent interest over a long period (years), it's likely that the niche is evergreen.
Future Relevance: Ask yourself, does this topic have future relevance? Evergreen niches often have an inherent longevity to them. Topics like education, health, personal finance, fitness, cooking, and travel tend to be evergreen because they'll always be relevant to people's lives.
Audience Demographics: Consider who your audience is. If your audience is a specific age group that will age out of your content, it might not be an evergreen niche. But if your content is appealing to a broad demographic range, it's more likely to be evergreen.
Inherent Characteristics of the Niche: Some niches are by nature more evergreen than others. For example, niches that rely on timely news or current events may not be as evergreen as niches that focus on timeless topics such as beauty and fashion or travel and lifestyle. 
Competitor Analysis: Look at other channels in your niche. If they have been successful for a long period, it's a good indication the niche is evergreen.
Rate of Change: If the core knowledge or skills in your niche change rapidly, it could be a trend. Evergreen content tends to revolve around knowledge or skills that stay relevant for longer periods.

Choosing an evergreen niche doesn't mean your content has to be static. Even within evergreen niches, trends will come and go. Successful YouTubers find ways to integrate trends into their content strategy to keep things fresh and engaging while maintaining their focus on evergreen topics.
Following these research methods can give you a better understanding of the level of demand and competition in your niche and help you make more informed decisions about the content you create for your YouTube channel.
Remember that balance is key! Passion, authority, high CPM, high affiliate potential and researching demand can help you create a sustainable and successful content strategy. Missing out on either one of these factors can be detrimental to your growth.
For instance, if you create content without passion, keeping only monetization in mind, you may feel disinterested after a while or even experience burnout. Whereas if you focus solely on a topic you’re passionate about, your content might not appeal to a wider audience, limiting your channel’s growth and earning potential. Similarly, if you lack authority in your niche, you won’t be able to create content that adds value, builds trust or stands out. Lack of trust or viewership can affect your earnings. 
Not considering CPM potential and high affiliate potential might lower your earnings. While your channel could see some success, it would make little to no money. Moreover, not finding relevant products to promote on your channel can hinder your ability to generate income through affiliate marketing.
Lastly, insufficient research could lead you to enter niches with little audience interest or too much competition, which can impact your growth as well as earnings. If there is no demand for your topic, you won’t get any views no matter how interesting your content is or how much authority you hold.

1. What Is A YouTube Niche?
Rather than a single topic, a YouTube niche refers to a specific category or subject matter that becomes the focus of your channel. It defines the type of content you produce consistently and helps you target a specific audience.
For instance, in this channel, Dad, How Do I, the creator shares ‘How To’ videos which are catered to teach people things that their Dad would. It falls under the broad niche of Educational Videos and is targeted to a specific audience. 
 
From the above example, we understand that having a niche on YouTube is crucial for several reasons. If you focus on a specific target audience with shared interests, it increases the likelihood of attracting loyal and engaged viewers. It also helps you establish a clear identity and positioning, making it easier for your viewers to understand what your channel is about.
Focusing on a specific niche gives you a clear direction for content creation and can even help you establish yourself as an expert on that particular niche. It can also attract advertisers and brands interested in your audience, which increases your opportunities for monetization.
Lastly, YouTube’s algorithms reward niche-focused channels. The more niched down your topic is, the easier it is for your videos to appear in relevant searches and recommendations, which ultimately leads to better content discovery.
2. How To Find Your Niche
While you might have different goals to start a YouTube channel, there are a few things you need to consider. Rather than putting in all your effort without a clear direction, you can ask yourself a few questions that will help you narrow down on a niche and build a successful YouTube channel. 

2.1. What Are You Passionate About?
Winning the YouTube game requires commitment and motivation over a long period of time. To ace the game, you would need approximately 100 or more videos. If you pick a niche you’re not passionate about, will you be able to deep dive into researching more about it or create content that resonates with your audience?
Passion is what fuels intrinsic motivation and keeps you committed in the face of challenges, setbacks or slow growth periods. It’s important to be passionate about the niche you choose because this deep interest can help you find creative solutions or generate ideas easily. For instance, if you are passionate about cooking, you can create videos about exploring different cuisines, recipes, cooking techniques and even do restaurant reviews.
Joshua Weissman does a fantastic job at this. On his eponymous channel that has over 8M subscribers, he not only shares cooking videos but also how to make cheaper alternatives of famous franchise foods at home as well as restaurant reviews.
 The best way to identify your passions is to list them down. You can do this by: 

Reflecting on your hobbies: What do you like to do during your free time? Is it playing a musical instrument, gaming or painting? 
Identifying childhood interests: Was there anything that excited you when you were a child? Is that activity still a part of your life like a sport you enjoy playing?
Going through your search history: What do you research the most online? What does your YouTube search history look like? What kind of content have you been consuming the most? Make a list of those things.
Asking your friends and family: During conversations with people close to you, there must be a topic you enjoy speaking about the most. Ask your friends and family what they think you’re passionate about. 

During this step of the process, do not think about whether or not your passion will make you money on YouTube. Simply list them down and think if you’d be interested in working on them for the next 2-3 years.
2.2. Can You Build Authority?
After you’ve listed down your passions, you need to narrow down on this list by seeing which of these passions you can build authority in. 
Building authority translates to showcasing your expertise, knowledge and establishing yourself as a credible source of information. When your viewers perceive you as an expert, they are more likely to trust and value your content. 
In a competitive YouTube landscape, having authority over your niche can help you get a dedicated following, higher engagement and more subscribers who seek trustworthy, well researched content.
Ahrefs, a SaaS company that creates online SEO tools for marketing professionals, share their knowledge and expertise by creating SEO tutorials, tips and share strategies on their YouTube channel.

While picking your niche based on passion and interest, make sure that you have the skill-set and knowledge to create the required content. Taking a cue from the example above, if you’re passionate about SEO or marketing but have limited knowledge, you will not be able to create well-informed, authoritative content like Ahrefs.
To figure out which passion can help you build authority, ask yourself: 

What are you good at? 
What are you experienced in? 
What topic do you have a natural talent for? 
What is something you’re most proficient in? 

If you have the answers to these questions, it will become easier to narrow down on an area of interest. Once you’re sure about the niche you are passionate about and can build authority in, it’s time to move towards the next step.
3. Can I Make Money From This?
This is one of the most crucial steps that people often miss when selecting a niche for YouTube. People often overlook monetization potential as they may be driven by their passion or interest. While passion and interest is essential, overlooking monetization can hinder long-term sustainability and growth.
Considering whether or not your niche can make money on YouTube ensures that your efforts can translate into some form of financial rewards and help you generate income. Understanding a niche’s earning possibilities helps you strike a balance between your passion and interest, and ensures that your channel is a profitable venture which can support your content creation journey in the long run.
3.1. How To Make Money From Your YouTube Channel
As a content creator, there are several ways you can make money with your YouTube Channel. These include advertising, affiliate marketing, brand sponsorships, fan funding and merchandise sales. Below are some ways in which you can monetize your channel. 
a. YouTube Partner Program 
The first step to earning money on YouTube begins with joining the YouTube Partner Program (YPP). This program gives content creators the ability to monetize their videos through Google AdSense.
To qualify for YPP, you will need to fulfill certain criteria: 

Have 1,000 subscribers
Either 4,000 valid public watch hours in the last 12 months or 10m valid public Shorts views in the last 90 days. 

This criteria remains the same for earning revenue through Ads as well as Premium Subscriptions. 
There are new lower thresholds for creators from US, UK, Canada, Taiwan and South Korea (coming to all countries where the YPP is available) to access fan funding features and Creator Support. This includes having:

500 subscribers
3 valid public uploads in the last 90 days
Either 3,000 valid public watch hours in the past year or 3m valid public Shorts views in the last 90 days

The new thresholds have been introduced specifically for small creators to apply sooner and start earning.
In addition to the above, you also need to: 

Adhere to YouTube’s monetisation policies 
Live in a country or region where the program is available
Have no active community guidelines strikes against your channel
Have a linked Google AdSense account

If you meet these requirements and get accepted as a YouTube Partner, there are several ways in which you can monetise your content. 

 Advertising: To run ads on your videos, you need to be at least 18 years old or have an adult guardian who can handle your payments via Google’s AdSense platform. You also need to create content that meets Google’s advertiser-friendly content guidelines
 Channel Memberships: YouTube Channel Memberships allow fans to support their favorite YouTubers by committing to automated monthly donations. In exchange, channel members might get access to member-only content, loyalty badges, and other unique perks. To gain access to the YouTube channel membership feature, your channel needs more than 30,000 subscribers and zero community guidelines violations on record. Once you gain access, you will see a Join button next to the Subscribe button



 Merchandise Shelf: You can make merchandise to market your content and sell it through YouTube’s integrated e-commerce feature known as Merch shelf. To qualify for Merch shelf access, you must be at least 18 years old, be a part of YPP, your audience isn’t set as Made For Kids and you have not violated any community guidelines. 
 Super Chat and Super Stickers: Super Chat and Super Stickers are features that let your viewers and fans purchase chat messages that stand out during live-streamed chats. To take advantage of Super Chat and Super Stickers, you need to be at least 18 years old and live in a country or region where they’re available.

3.2. Youtube CPM
CPM stands for Cost Per Mille, where Mille refers to one thousand impressions. It represents the revenue generated by a video creator for every one thousand ad impressions that their videos receive.
While the earning potential of a YouTube channel is influenced by various factors, understanding how your niche can influence CPM earnings can help you monetize your content effectively.
Some niches attract advertisers who are willing to pay a premium for targeted audiences or certain audience demographics they might be looking for. For instance, content related to finance, lifestyle, or fashion may have higher CPMs compared to more general content such as dance or music covers.
If your niche is high in demand among advertisers, you may experience higher CPMs as they compete for ad placements on your videos. This essentially means you’ll be generating a higher revenue for the views you receive on your videos.

4. How Do I Research My Niche?
Before you choose a niche for your YouTube channel, it is important to do a thorough demand,  competition & longevity analysis. Researching audience demand and preferences helps you tailor your content to meet their needs and interests.
A thorough research of the competition helps you identify gaps and opportunities while selecting the best niche for YouTube. By understanding your niche and the competition, you can develop a strategy to stand out and make your content unique. It will also help you understand the monetizing potential of your niche which can help you generate more income. 
There are several methods you can use to research demand and competition while choosing the best niche for YouTube. 
4.1. Conduct Keyword Research
Use keyword research tools such as Google Keyword Planner, the YouTube search bar, Google Trends, and VidIQ to identify popular search terms associated with your niche. See if they have high search volumes and consistent interest. It can help you understand your niche or interest’s potential value. 
You can use the following methods to conduct keyword research 
Youtube search method/Alphabet soup
To do keyword and topic research for a niche via the YouTube search bar, follow these steps:

Type a broad keyword related to your niche in the YouTube search bar
Look at the suggested search terms that appear below the search bar, as this can give you an idea of what people are searching for related to your niche



Scroll through the search results and look at the titles and descriptions of the top videos to see what topics are popular in your niche
Look at the number of views, likes, and comments on the top videos to gauge the level of interest in those topics
Use the "Filter" option on the search results page to narrow down the results by upload date, view count, and other criteria to find more specific topics and trends in your niche

Google Trends Method 
Google Trends is a tool that can be used to analyze the popularity of search terms over time. To use Google Trends for keyword and topic research for YouTube, follow these steps:

Visit Google Trends 
Enter a broad keyword related to your niche in the search bar



Use the filters below your keyword at the top of the page to narrow down the results by location, time period, and category (e.g., Arts & Entertainment, Sports, etc.)



Look at the "Interest over time" graph to see how the popularity of the keyword has changed over time



Scroll down to the "Related queries" section to see other search terms that are related to your keyword



Click on a related query to see its "Interest over time" graph and related queries
Repeat the process for each related query to find new topics and search terms to explore

VidIQ 
VidIQ can help you find relevant and high-ranking keywords associated with videos. To do a keyword research on VidIQ, follow these steps: 

Start by installing the VidIQ browser extension for Chrome or Firefox. You can find the extension on the respective web stores and add it to your browser
Go to YouTube and you will see the VidIQ extension icon in your browser at the top right. Click the drop down icon to open the menu
In the VidIQ panel, click on the Keyword Inspector option. Here, you'll find various keyword suggestions related to the video's topic 



In Keyword Inspector, type in your broad keyword and hit search to get your results. VidIQ assigns scores to each keyword, indicating its potential value. Pay attention to the Search volume, Competition, and Overall score to assess the keyword's viability.


You can do this much by accessing VidIQ’s free extension. VidIQ Pro offers more features but you might not need it for basic keyword research. 
Google keyword planner
Google Keyword Planner can help you gain valuable insights into the search volume and competition level for keywords related to your niche. Follow these steps to use it:   

Go to the Google Keyword Planner website and log in with your Google account
Click on "Discover new keywords" and enter a broad keyword related to your niche
Specify your targeting options, such as location and language
Click "Get results" to generate a list of keywords related to your niche
Sort the list by relevance, search volume, or other criteria to find the most relevant keywords for your niche
Click on a keyword to see additional data, such as search volume trends and competition level
Use the keyword data to inform your content strategy, including video titles, tags, and descriptions.

4.2. Analyze Competition
Apart from keyword research, you also need to analyze the competition for your niche on YouTube. Visit the channels of your top competitors and examine their statistics such as subscriber count, total video views as well as engagement metrics such as likes, comments and shares. 
Analyzing the comments section of your competition’s videos can help you get insights into audience preference and content gaps. For instance, check out these comments on Marques Brownlee’s iPhone 14 review on YouTube. You get a fair idea that the content he is sharing is informative and appreciated by his audience. 

Make sure you watch several videos as well to understand your competition’s content strategy. Take a look at the videos they produce, their format and the topics they cover. You can then gauge what works and what doesn’t.
Going through your competitions videos will also help you understand if they have collaborated with other creators, companies or brands and how well affiliate marketing or brand sponsorships work for them.
Based on your analysis, you can identify gaps and opportunities which can help you plan your strategy and create meaningful content. 
4.3. Use Social Media
You can use social media to analyze a niche for YouTube to gain valuable insights into audience interest, engagement and trends. Identify key platforms which are relevant for your niche. 
While Facebook, Instagram, Twitter and TikTok are popular platforms to start with, you might want to check out the other platforms where your audience spends its time. For instance, if your niche is talking about everything NFT, then you might want to check out platforms such as Telegram, Discord and Reddit. 
Social media platforms are also a great way to keep an eye on trending topics within your niche and help you get insights into current interests and popular discussions. 
4.4. Survey Your Audience
Once you have a small following, you can survey your audience to understand their preferences and interests. This can help you tailor your content to their needs and preferences and build a loyal following.
Apart from encouraging your audience to leave suggestions, opinions or feedback in the comments section and engaging with them there, here are a few other ways in which you can survey your audience:

Community Tab: If your channel is eligible, you can use the Community Tab feature to post polls and questions directly to your subscribers
Video Poll Cards: During your videos, use YouTube's interactive poll cards. These are on-screen annotations that allow viewers to vote on a specific question while watching your video
Video End Screens: Use end screens to prompt viewers to take a survey or participate in a poll related to the video they just watched

4.5. Real World Research
While online research is important, don’t miss out on real world experience and identifying potential gaps in the market you can capitalize on. It could be a gap in a field you’re working in or it could be from a real life experience. 
For instance, Cassey Ho, the founder of Blogilates started her channel by creating online pilates videos for her students. As she was moving away from her hometown, she didn’t want her students to miss out and at the time, roughly around 2009, there was a gap in the market for an online pilates instructor. Since then, her POP Pilates videos have garnered over millions of views.
If you already have real-world proof that your content or services are needed, you can start from there itself. Filling in gaps with valuable and relevant content allows you to position your channel uniquely and attract a dedicated audience seeking the specific information or service you provide.
4.6. Longevity Test
If you have zeroed in on a niche, it’s important to check its longevity too. Is it just a passing trend or is it evergreen? Here are several things you can do to verify the longevity of a niche.

Historical Consistency: Use tools like Google Trends, YouTube's own search tools, or specialized SEO tools to analyze the historical search volume and interest for topics in your niche. If there is consistent interest over a long period (years), it's likely that the niche is evergreen.
Future Relevance: Ask yourself, does this topic have future relevance? Evergreen niches often have an inherent longevity to them. Topics like education, health, personal finance, fitness, cooking, and travel tend to be evergreen because they'll always be relevant to people's lives.
Audience Demographics: Consider who your audience is. If your audience is a specific age group that will age out of your content, it might not be an evergreen niche. But if your content is appealing to a broad demographic range, it's more likely to be evergreen.
Inherent Characteristics of the Niche: Some niches are by nature more evergreen than others. For example, niches that rely on timely news or current events may not be as evergreen as niches that focus on timeless topics such as beauty and fashion or travel and lifestyle. 
Competitor Analysis: Look at other channels in your niche. If they have been successful for a long period, it's a good indication the niche is evergreen.
Rate of Change: If the core knowledge or skills in your niche change rapidly, it could be a trend. Evergreen content tends to revolve around knowledge or skills that stay relevant for longer periods.

Choosing an evergreen niche doesn't mean your content has to be static. Even within evergreen niches, trends will come and go. Successful YouTubers find ways to integrate trends into their content strategy to keep things fresh and engaging while maintaining their focus on evergreen topics.
Following these research methods can give you a better understanding of the level of demand and competition in your niche and help you make more informed decisions about the content you create for your YouTube channel.
Remember that balance is key! Passion, authority, high CPM, high affiliate potential and researching demand can help you create a sustainable and successful content strategy. Missing out on either one of these factors can be detrimental to your growth.
For instance, if you create content without passion, keeping only monetization in mind, you may feel disinterested after a while or even experience burnout. Whereas if you focus solely on a topic you’re passionate about, your content might not appeal to a wider audience, limiting your channel’s growth and earning potential. Similarly, if you lack authority in your niche, you won’t be able to create content that adds value, builds trust or stands out. Lack of trust or viewership can affect your earnings. 
Not considering CPM potential and high affiliate potential might lower your earnings. While your channel could see some success, it would make little to no money. Moreover, not finding relevant products to promote on your channel can hinder your ability to generate income through affiliate marketing.
Lastly, insufficient research could lead you to enter niches with little audience interest or too much competition, which can impact your growth as well as earnings. If there is no demand for your topic, you won’t get any views no matter how interesting your content is or how much authority you hold.

1. What Is A YouTube Niche?
Rather than a single topic, a YouTube niche refers to a specific category or subject matter that becomes the focus of your channel. It defines the type of content you produce consistently and helps you target a specific audience.
For instance, in this channel, Dad, How Do I, the creator shares ‘How To’ videos which are catered to teach people things that their Dad would. It falls under the broad niche of Educational Videos and is targeted to a specific audience. 
 
From the above example, we understand that having a niche on YouTube is crucial for several reasons. If you focus on a specific target audience with shared interests, it increases the likelihood of attracting loyal and engaged viewers. It also helps you establish a clear identity and positioning, making it easier for your viewers to understand what your channel is about.
Focusing on a specific niche gives you a clear direction for content creation and can even help you establish yourself as an expert on that particular niche. It can also attract advertisers and brands interested in your audience, which increases your opportunities for monetization.
Lastly, YouTube’s algorithms reward niche-focused channels. The more niched down your topic is, the easier it is for your videos to appear in relevant searches and recommendations, which ultimately leads to better content discovery.
2. How To Find Your Niche
While you might have different goals to start a YouTube channel, there are a few things you need to consider. Rather than putting in all your effort without a clear direction, you can ask yourself a few questions that will help you narrow down on a niche and build a successful YouTube channel. 

2.1. What Are You Passionate About?
Winning the YouTube game requires commitment and motivation over a long period of time. To ace the game, you would need approximately 100 or more videos. If you pick a niche you’re not passionate about, will you be able to deep dive into researching more about it or create content that resonates with your audience?
Passion is what fuels intrinsic motivation and keeps you committed in the face of challenges, setbacks or slow growth periods. It’s important to be passionate about the niche you choose because this deep interest can help you find creative solutions or generate ideas easily. For instance, if you are passionate about cooking, you can create videos about exploring different cuisines, recipes, cooking techniques and even do restaurant reviews.
Joshua Weissman does a fantastic job at this. On his eponymous channel that has over 8M subscribers, he not only shares cooking videos but also how to make cheaper alternatives of famous franchise foods at home as well as restaurant reviews.
 The best way to identify your passions is to list them down. You can do this by: 

Reflecting on your hobbies: What do you like to do during your free time? Is it playing a musical instrument, gaming or painting? 
Identifying childhood interests: Was there anything that excited you when you were a child? Is that activity still a part of your life like a sport you enjoy playing?
Going through your search history: What do you research the most online? What does your YouTube search history look like? What kind of content have you been consuming the most? Make a list of those things.
Asking your friends and family: During conversations with people close to you, there must be a topic you enjoy speaking about the most. Ask your friends and family what they think you’re passionate about. 

During this step of the process, do not think about whether or not your passion will make you money on YouTube. Simply list them down and think if you’d be interested in working on them for the next 2-3 years.
2.2. Can You Build Authority?
After you’ve listed down your passions, you need to narrow down on this list by seeing which of these passions you can build authority in. 
Building authority translates to showcasing your expertise, knowledge and establishing yourself as a credible source of information. When your viewers perceive you as an expert, they are more likely to trust and value your content. 
In a competitive YouTube landscape, having authority over your niche can help you get a dedicated following, higher engagement and more subscribers who seek trustworthy, well researched content.
Ahrefs, a SaaS company that creates online SEO tools for marketing professionals, share their knowledge and expertise by creating SEO tutorials, tips and share strategies on their YouTube channel.

While picking your niche based on passion and interest, make sure that you have the skill-set and knowledge to create the required content. Taking a cue from the example above, if you’re passionate about SEO or marketing but have limited knowledge, you will not be able to create well-informed, authoritative content like Ahrefs.
To figure out which passion can help you build authority, ask yourself: 

What are you good at? 
What are you experienced in? 
What topic do you have a natural talent for? 
What is something you’re most proficient in? 

If you have the answers to these questions, it will become easier to narrow down on an area of interest. Once you’re sure about the niche you are passionate about and can build authority in, it’s time to move towards the next step.
3. Can I Make Money From This?
This is one of the most crucial steps that people often miss when selecting a niche for YouTube. People often overlook monetization potential as they may be driven by their passion or interest. While passion and interest is essential, overlooking monetization can hinder long-term sustainability and growth.
Considering whether or not your niche can make money on YouTube ensures that your efforts can translate into some form of financial rewards and help you generate income. Understanding a niche’s earning possibilities helps you strike a balance between your passion and interest, and ensures that your channel is a profitable venture which can support your content creation journey in the long run.
3.1. How To Make Money From Your YouTube Channel
As a content creator, there are several ways you can make money with your YouTube Channel. These include advertising, affiliate marketing, brand sponsorships, fan funding and merchandise sales. Below are some ways in which you can monetize your channel. 
a. YouTube Partner Program 
The first step to earning money on YouTube begins with joining the YouTube Partner Program (YPP). This program gives content creators the ability to monetize their videos through Google AdSense.
To qualify for YPP, you will need to fulfill certain criteria: 

Have 1,000 subscribers
Either 4,000 valid public watch hours in the last 12 months or 10m valid public Shorts views in the last 90 days. 

This criteria remains the same for earning revenue through Ads as well as Premium Subscriptions. 
There are new lower thresholds for creators from US, UK, Canada, Taiwan and South Korea (coming to all countries where the YPP is available) to access fan funding features and Creator Support. This includes having:

500 subscribers
3 valid public uploads in the last 90 days
Either 3,000 valid public watch hours in the past year or 3m valid public Shorts views in the last 90 days

The new thresholds have been introduced specifically for small creators to apply sooner and start earning.
In addition to the above, you also need to: 

Adhere to YouTube’s monetisation policies 
Live in a country or region where the program is available
Have no active community guidelines strikes against your channel
Have a linked Google AdSense account

If you meet these requirements and get accepted as a YouTube Partner, there are several ways in which you can monetise your content. 

 Advertising: To run ads on your videos, you need to be at least 18 years old or have an adult guardian who can handle your payments via Google’s AdSense platform. You also need to create content that meets Google’s advertiser-friendly content guidelines
 Channel Memberships: YouTube Channel Memberships allow fans to support their favorite YouTubers by committing to automated monthly donations. In exchange, channel members might get access to member-only content, loyalty badges, and other unique perks. To gain access to the YouTube channel membership feature, your channel needs more than 30,000 subscribers and zero community guidelines violations on record. Once you gain access, you will see a Join button next to the Subscribe button



 Merchandise Shelf: You can make merchandise to market your content and sell it through YouTube’s integrated e-commerce feature known as Merch shelf. To qualify for Merch shelf access, you must be at least 18 years old, be a part of YPP, your audience isn’t set as Made For Kids and you have not violated any community guidelines. 
 Super Chat and Super Stickers: Super Chat and Super Stickers are features that let your viewers and fans purchase chat messages that stand out during live-streamed chats. To take advantage of Super Chat and Super Stickers, you need to be at least 18 years old and live in a country or region where they’re available.

b. Affiliate Marketing
Affiliate marketing through Youtube is an intelligent approach to give your viewers more value while also generating income. It gives you direct control over what you are promoting. 
YouTube affiliate marketing is simply the process of promoting products or services on YouTube by creating videos around them or organically integrating them in your content and earning a commission whenever someone makes a purchase or clicks on your affiliate link.
As an affiliate, you can promote anything from apps, softwares, books, shoes, shirts, jeans, electronics, medicines, beauty products, baby products, and groceries to financial products. You can approach different companies like Amazon or InVideo who offer affiliate programs.

3.2. Youtube CPM
CPM stands for Cost Per Mille, where Mille refers to one thousand impressions. It represents the revenue generated by a video creator for every one thousand ad impressions that their videos receive.
While the earning potential of a YouTube channel is influenced by various factors, understanding how your niche can influence CPM earnings can help you monetize your content effectively.
Some niches attract advertisers who are willing to pay a premium for targeted audiences or certain audience demographics they might be looking for. For instance, content related to finance, lifestyle, or fashion may have higher CPMs compared to more general content such as dance or music covers.
If your niche is high in demand among advertisers, you may experience higher CPMs as they compete for ad placements on your videos. This essentially means you’ll be generating a higher revenue for the views you receive on your videos.

4. How Do I Research My Niche?
Before you choose a niche for your YouTube channel, it is important to do a thorough demand,  competition & longevity analysis. Researching audience demand and preferences helps you tailor your content to meet their needs and interests.
A thorough research of the competition helps you identify gaps and opportunities while selecting the best niche for YouTube. By understanding your niche and the competition, you can develop a strategy to stand out and make your content unique. It will also help you understand the monetizing potential of your niche which can help you generate more income. 
There are several methods you can use to research demand and competition while choosing the best niche for YouTube. 
4.1. Conduct Keyword Research
Use keyword research tools such as Google Keyword Planner, the YouTube search bar, Google Trends, and VidIQ to identify popular search terms associated with your niche. See if they have high search volumes and consistent interest. It can help you understand your niche or interest’s potential value. 
You can use the following methods to conduct keyword research 
Youtube search method/Alphabet soup
To do keyword and topic research for a niche via the YouTube search bar, follow these steps:

Type a broad keyword related to your niche in the YouTube search bar
Look at the suggested search terms that appear below the search bar, as this can give you an idea of what people are searching for related to your niche



Scroll through the search results and look at the titles and descriptions of the top videos to see what topics are popular in your niche
Look at the number of views, likes, and comments on the top videos to gauge the level of interest in those topics
Use the "Filter" option on the search results page to narrow down the results by upload date, view count, and other criteria to find more specific topics and trends in your niche

Google Trends Method 
Google Trends is a tool that can be used to analyze the popularity of search terms over time. To use Google Trends for keyword and topic research for YouTube, follow these steps:

Visit Google Trends 
Enter a broad keyword related to your niche in the search bar



Use the filters below your keyword at the top of the page to narrow down the results by location, time period, and category (e.g., Arts & Entertainment, Sports, etc.)



Look at the "Interest over time" graph to see how the popularity of the keyword has changed over time



Scroll down to the "Related queries" section to see other search terms that are related to your keyword



Click on a related query to see its "Interest over time" graph and related queries
Repeat the process for each related query to find new topics and search terms to explore

VidIQ 
VidIQ can help you find relevant and high-ranking keywords associated with videos. To do a keyword research on VidIQ, follow these steps: 

Start by installing the VidIQ browser extension for Chrome or Firefox. You can find the extension on the respective web stores and add it to your browser
Go to YouTube and you will see the VidIQ extension icon in your browser at the top right. Click the drop down icon to open the menu
In the VidIQ panel, click on the Keyword Inspector option. Here, you'll find various keyword suggestions related to the video's topic 



In Keyword Inspector, type in your broad keyword and hit search to get your results. VidIQ assigns scores to each keyword, indicating its potential value. Pay attention to the Search volume, Competition, and Overall score to assess the keyword's viability.


You can do this much by accessing VidIQ’s free extension. VidIQ Pro offers more features but you might not need it for basic keyword research. 
Google keyword planner
Google Keyword Planner can help you gain valuable insights into the search volume and competition level for keywords related to your niche. Follow these steps to use it:   

Go to the Google Keyword Planner website and log in with your Google account
Click on "Discover new keywords" and enter a broad keyword related to your niche
Specify your targeting options, such as location and language
Click "Get results" to generate a list of keywords related to your niche
Sort the list by relevance, search volume, or other criteria to find the most relevant keywords for your niche
Click on a keyword to see additional data, such as search volume trends and competition level
Use the keyword data to inform your content strategy, including video titles, tags, and descriptions.

4.2. Analyze Competition
Apart from keyword research, you also need to analyze the competition for your niche on YouTube. Visit the channels of your top competitors and examine their statistics such as subscriber count, total video views as well as engagement metrics such as likes, comments and shares. 
Analyzing the comments section of your competition’s videos can help you get insights into audience preference and content gaps. For instance, check out these comments on Marques Brownlee’s iPhone 14 review on YouTube. You get a fair idea that the content he is sharing is informative and appreciated by his audience. 

Make sure you watch several videos as well to understand your competition’s content strategy. Take a look at the videos they produce, their format and the topics they cover. You can then gauge what works and what doesn’t.
Going through your competitions videos will also help you understand if they have collaborated with other creators, companies or brands and how well affiliate marketing or brand sponsorships work for them.
Based on your analysis, you can identify gaps and opportunities which can help you plan your strategy and create meaningful content. 
4.3. Use Social Media
You can use social media to analyze a niche for YouTube to gain valuable insights into audience interest, engagement and trends. Identify key platforms which are relevant for your niche. 
While Facebook, Instagram, Twitter and TikTok are popular platforms to start with, you might want to check out the other platforms where your audience spends its time. For instance, if your niche is talking about everything NFT, then you might want to check out platforms such as Telegram, Discord and Reddit. 
Social media platforms are also a great way to keep an eye on trending topics within your niche and help you get insights into current interests and popular discussions. 
4.4. Survey Your Audience
Once you have a small following, you can survey your audience to understand their preferences and interests. This can help you tailor your content to their needs and preferences and build a loyal following.
Apart from encouraging your audience to leave suggestions, opinions or feedback in the comments section and engaging with them there, here are a few other ways in which you can survey your audience:

Community Tab: If your channel is eligible, you can use the Community Tab feature to post polls and questions directly to your subscribers
Video Poll Cards: During your videos, use YouTube's interactive poll cards. These are on-screen annotations that allow viewers to vote on a specific question while watching your video
Video End Screens: Use end screens to prompt viewers to take a survey or participate in a poll related to the video they just watched

4.5. Real World Research
While online research is important, don’t miss out on real world experience and identifying potential gaps in the market you can capitalize on. It could be a gap in a field you’re working in or it could be from a real life experience. 
For instance, Cassey Ho, the founder of Blogilates started her channel by creating online pilates videos for her students. As she was moving away from her hometown, she didn’t want her students to miss out and at the time, roughly around 2009, there was a gap in the market for an online pilates instructor. Since then, her POP Pilates videos have garnered over millions of views.
If you already have real-world proof that your content or services are needed, you can start from there itself. Filling in gaps with valuable and relevant content allows you to position your channel uniquely and attract a dedicated audience seeking the specific information or service you provide.
4.6. Longevity Test
If you have zeroed in on a niche, it’s important to check its longevity too. Is it just a passing trend or is it evergreen? Here are several things you can do to verify the longevity of a niche.

Historical Consistency: Use tools like Google Trends, YouTube's own search tools, or specialized SEO tools to analyze the historical search volume and interest for topics in your niche. If there is consistent interest over a long period (years), it's likely that the niche is evergreen.
Future Relevance: Ask yourself, does this topic have future relevance? Evergreen niches often have an inherent longevity to them. Topics like education, health, personal finance, fitness, cooking, and travel tend to be evergreen because they'll always be relevant to people's lives.
Audience Demographics: Consider who your audience is. If your audience is a specific age group that will age out of your content, it might not be an evergreen niche. But if your content is appealing to a broad demographic range, it's more likely to be evergreen.
Inherent Characteristics of the Niche: Some niches are by nature more evergreen than others. For example, niches that rely on timely news or current events may not be as evergreen as niches that focus on timeless topics such as beauty and fashion or travel and lifestyle. 
Competitor Analysis: Look at other channels in your niche. If they have been successful for a long period, it's a good indication the niche is evergreen.
Rate of Change: If the core knowledge or skills in your niche change rapidly, it could be a trend. Evergreen content tends to revolve around knowledge or skills that stay relevant for longer periods.

Choosing an evergreen niche doesn't mean your content has to be static. Even within evergreen niches, trends will come and go. Successful YouTubers find ways to integrate trends into their content strategy to keep things fresh and engaging while maintaining their focus on evergreen topics.
Following these research methods can give you a better understanding of the level of demand and competition in your niche and help you make more informed decisions about the content you create for your YouTube channel.
Remember that balance is key! Passion, authority, high CPM, high affiliate potential and researching demand can help you create a sustainable and successful content strategy. Missing out on either one of these factors can be detrimental to your growth.
For instance, if you create content without passion, keeping only monetization in mind, you may feel disinterested after a while or even experience burnout. Whereas if you focus solely on a topic you’re passionate about, your content might not appeal to a wider audience, limiting your channel’s growth and earning potential. Similarly, if you lack authority in your niche, you won’t be able to create content that adds value, builds trust or stands out. Lack of trust or viewership can affect your earnings. 
Not considering CPM potential and high affiliate potential might lower your earnings. While your channel could see some success, it would make little to no money. Moreover, not finding relevant products to promote on your channel can hinder your ability to generate income through affiliate marketing.
Lastly, insufficient research could lead you to enter niches with little audience interest or too much competition, which can impact your growth as well as earnings. If there is no demand for your topic, you won’t get any views no matter how interesting your content is or how much authority you hold.

1. What Is A YouTube Niche?
Rather than a single topic, a YouTube niche refers to a specific category or subject matter that becomes the focus of your channel. It defines the type of content you produce consistently and helps you target a specific audience.
For instance, in this channel, Dad, How Do I, the creator shares ‘How To’ videos which are catered to teach people things that their Dad would. It falls under the broad niche of Educational Videos and is targeted to a specific audience. 
 
From the above example, we understand that having a niche on YouTube is crucial for several reasons. If you focus on a specific target audience with shared interests, it increases the likelihood of attracting loyal and engaged viewers. It also helps you establish a clear identity and positioning, making it easier for your viewers to understand what your channel is about.
Focusing on a specific niche gives you a clear direction for content creation and can even help you establish yourself as an expert on that particular niche. It can also attract advertisers and brands interested in your audience, which increases your opportunities for monetization.
Lastly, YouTube’s algorithms reward niche-focused channels. The more niched down your topic is, the easier it is for your videos to appear in relevant searches and recommendations, which ultimately leads to better content discovery.
2. How To Find Your Niche
While you might have different goals to start a YouTube channel, there are a few things you need to consider. Rather than putting in all your effort without a clear direction, you can ask yourself a few questions that will help you narrow down on a niche and build a successful YouTube channel. 

2.1. What Are You Passionate About?
Winning the YouTube game requires commitment and motivation over a long period of time. To ace the game, you would need approximately 100 or more videos. If you pick a niche you’re not passionate about, will you be able to deep dive into researching more about it or create content that resonates with your audience?
Passion is what fuels intrinsic motivation and keeps you committed in the face of challenges, setbacks or slow growth periods. It’s important to be passionate about the niche you choose because this deep interest can help you find creative solutions or generate ideas easily. For instance, if you are passionate about cooking, you can create videos about exploring different cuisines, recipes, cooking techniques and even do restaurant reviews.
Joshua Weissman does a fantastic job at this. On his eponymous channel that has over 8M subscribers, he not only shares cooking videos but also how to make cheaper alternatives of famous franchise foods at home as well as restaurant reviews.
 The best way to identify your passions is to list them down. You can do this by: 

Reflecting on your hobbies: What do you like to do during your free time? Is it playing a musical instrument, gaming or painting? 
Identifying childhood interests: Was there anything that excited you when you were a child? Is that activity still a part of your life like a sport you enjoy playing?
Going through your search history: What do you research the most online? What does your YouTube search history look like? What kind of content have you been consuming the most? Make a list of those things.
Asking your friends and family: During conversations with people close to you, there must be a topic you enjoy speaking about the most. Ask your friends and family what they think you’re passionate about. 

During this step of the process, do not think about whether or not your passion will make you money on YouTube. Simply list them down and think if you’d be interested in working on them for the next 2-3 years.
2.2. Can You Build Authority?
After you’ve listed down your passions, you need to narrow down on this list by seeing which of these passions you can build authority in. 
Building authority translates to showcasing your expertise, knowledge and establishing yourself as a credible source of information. When your viewers perceive you as an expert, they are more likely to trust and value your content. 
In a competitive YouTube landscape, having authority over your niche can help you get a dedicated following, higher engagement and more subscribers who seek trustworthy, well researched content.
Ahrefs, a SaaS company that creates online SEO tools for marketing professionals, share their knowledge and expertise by creating SEO tutorials, tips and share strategies on their YouTube channel.

While picking your niche based on passion and interest, make sure that you have the skill-set and knowledge to create the required content. Taking a cue from the example above, if you’re passionate about SEO or marketing but have limited knowledge, you will not be able to create well-informed, authoritative content like Ahrefs.
To figure out which passion can help you build authority, ask yourself: 

What are you good at? 
What are you experienced in? 
What topic do you have a natural talent for? 
What is something you’re most proficient in? 

If you have the answers to these questions, it will become easier to narrow down on an area of interest. Once you’re sure about the niche you are passionate about and can build authority in, it’s time to move towards the next step.

3.1. How To Make Money From Your YouTube Channel
As a content creator, there are several ways you can make money with your YouTube Channel. These include advertising, affiliate marketing, brand sponsorships, fan funding and merchandise sales. Below are some ways in which you can monetize your channel. 
a. YouTube Partner Program 
The first step to earning money on YouTube begins with joining the YouTube Partner Program (YPP). This program gives content creators the ability to monetize their videos through Google AdSense.
To qualify for YPP, you will need to fulfill certain criteria: 

Have 1,000 subscribers
Either 4,000 valid public watch hours in the last 12 months or 10m valid public Shorts views in the last 90 days. 

This criteria remains the same for earning revenue through Ads as well as Premium Subscriptions. 
There are new lower thresholds for creators from US, UK, Canada, Taiwan and South Korea (coming to all countries where the YPP is available) to access fan funding features and Creator Support. This includes having:

500 subscribers
3 valid public uploads in the last 90 days
Either 3,000 valid public watch hours in the past year or 3m valid public Shorts views in the last 90 days

The new thresholds have been introduced specifically for small creators to apply sooner and start earning.
In addition to the above, you also need to: 

Adhere to YouTube’s monetisation policies 
Live in a country or region where the program is available
Have no active community guidelines strikes against your channel
Have a linked Google AdSense account

If you meet these requirements and get accepted as a YouTube Partner, there are several ways in which you can monetise your content. 

 Advertising: To run ads on your videos, you need to be at least 18 years old or have an adult guardian who can handle your payments via Google’s AdSense platform. You also need to create content that meets Google’s advertiser-friendly content guidelines
 Channel Memberships: YouTube Channel Memberships allow fans to support their favorite YouTubers by committing to automated monthly donations. In exchange, channel members might get access to member-only content, loyalty badges, and other unique perks. To gain access to the YouTube channel membership feature, your channel needs more than 30,000 subscribers and zero community guidelines violations on record. Once you gain access, you will see a Join button next to the Subscribe button



 Merchandise Shelf: You can make merchandise to market your content and sell it through YouTube’s integrated e-commerce feature known as Merch shelf. To qualify for Merch shelf access, you must be at least 18 years old, be a part of YPP, your audience isn’t set as Made For Kids and you have not violated any community guidelines. 
 Super Chat and Super Stickers: Super Chat and Super Stickers are features that let your viewers and fans purchase chat messages that stand out during live-streamed chats. To take advantage of Super Chat and Super Stickers, you need to be at least 18 years old and live in a country or region where they’re available.

3.2. Youtube CPM
CPM stands for Cost Per Mille, where Mille refers to one thousand impressions. It represents the revenue generated by a video creator for every one thousand ad impressions that their videos receive.
While the earning potential of a YouTube channel is influenced by various factors, understanding how your niche can influence CPM earnings can help you monetize your content effectively.
Some niches attract advertisers who are willing to pay a premium for targeted audiences or certain audience demographics they might be looking for. For instance, content related to finance, lifestyle, or fashion may have higher CPMs compared to more general content such as dance or music covers.
If your niche is high in demand among advertisers, you may experience higher CPMs as they compete for ad placements on your videos. This essentially means you’ll be generating a higher revenue for the views you receive on your videos.

4.1. Conduct Keyword Research
Use keyword research tools such as Google Keyword Planner, the YouTube search bar, Google Trends, and VidIQ to identify popular search terms associated with your niche. See if they have high search volumes and consistent interest. It can help you understand your niche or interest’s potential value. 
You can use the following methods to conduct keyword research 
Youtube search method/Alphabet soup
To do keyword and topic research for a niche via the YouTube search bar, follow these steps:

Type a broad keyword related to your niche in the YouTube search bar
Look at the suggested search terms that appear below the search bar, as this can give you an idea of what people are searching for related to your niche



Scroll through the search results and look at the titles and descriptions of the top videos to see what topics are popular in your niche
Look at the number of views, likes, and comments on the top videos to gauge the level of interest in those topics
Use the "Filter" option on the search results page to narrow down the results by upload date, view count, and other criteria to find more specific topics and trends in your niche

Google Trends Method 
Google Trends is a tool that can be used to analyze the popularity of search terms over time. To use Google Trends for keyword and topic research for YouTube, follow these steps:

Visit Google Trends 
Enter a broad keyword related to your niche in the search bar



Use the filters below your keyword at the top of the page to narrow down the results by location, time period, and category (e.g., Arts & Entertainment, Sports, etc.)



Look at the "Interest over time" graph to see how the popularity of the keyword has changed over time



Scroll down to the "Related queries" section to see other search terms that are related to your keyword



Click on a related query to see its "Interest over time" graph and related queries
Repeat the process for each related query to find new topics and search terms to explore

Click on "Discover new keywords" and enter a broad keyword related to your niche
Specify your targeting options, such as location and language
Click "Get results" to generate a list of keywords related to your niche
Sort the list by relevance, search volume, or other criteria to find the most relevant keywords for your niche
Click on a keyword to see additional data, such as search volume trends and competition level
Use the keyword data to inform your content strategy, including video titles, tags, and descriptions.

4.2. Analyze Competition
Apart from keyword research, you also need to analyze the competition for your niche on YouTube. Visit the channels of your top competitors and examine their statistics such as subscriber count, total video views as well as engagement metrics such as likes, comments and shares. 
Analyzing the comments section of your competition’s videos can help you get insights into audience preference and content gaps. For instance, check out these comments on Marques Brownlee’s iPhone 14 review on YouTube. You get a fair idea that the content he is sharing is informative and appreciated by his audience. 

Make sure you watch several videos as well to understand your competition’s content strategy. Take a look at the videos they produce, their format and the topics they cover. You can then gauge what works and what doesn’t.
Going through your competitions videos will also help you understand if they have collaborated with other creators, companies or brands and how well affiliate marketing or brand sponsorships work for them.
Based on your analysis, you can identify gaps and opportunities which can help you plan your strategy and create meaningful content. 
4.3. Use Social Media
You can use social media to analyze a niche for YouTube to gain valuable insights into audience interest, engagement and trends. Identify key platforms which are relevant for your niche. 
While Facebook, Instagram, Twitter and TikTok are popular platforms to start with, you might want to check out the other platforms where your audience spends its time. For instance, if your niche is talking about everything NFT, then you might want to check out platforms such as Telegram, Discord and Reddit. 
Social media platforms are also a great way to keep an eye on trending topics within your niche and help you get insights into current interests and popular discussions. 
4.4. Survey Your Audience
Once you have a small following, you can survey your audience to understand their preferences and interests. This can help you tailor your content to their needs and preferences and build a loyal following.
Apart from encouraging your audience to leave suggestions, opinions or feedback in the comments section and engaging with them there, here are a few other ways in which you can survey your audience:

Community Tab: If your channel is eligible, you can use the Community Tab feature to post polls and questions directly to your subscribers
Video Poll Cards: During your videos, use YouTube's interactive poll cards. These are on-screen annotations that allow viewers to vote on a specific question while watching your video
Video End Screens: Use end screens to prompt viewers to take a survey or participate in a poll related to the video they just watched

4.5. Real World Research
While online research is important, don’t miss out on real world experience and identifying potential gaps in the market you can capitalize on. It could be a gap in a field you’re working in or it could be from a real life experience. 
For instance, Cassey Ho, the founder of Blogilates started her channel by creating online pilates videos for her students. As she was moving away from her hometown, she didn’t want her students to miss out and at the time, roughly around 2009, there was a gap in the market for an online pilates instructor. Since then, her POP Pilates videos have garnered over millions of views.
If you already have real-world proof that your content or services are needed, you can start from there itself. Filling in gaps with valuable and relevant content allows you to position your channel uniquely and attract a dedicated audience seeking the specific information or service you provide.
4.6. Longevity Test
If you have zeroed in on a niche, it’s important to check its longevity too. Is it just a passing trend or is it evergreen? Here are several things you can do to verify the longevity of a niche.

Historical Consistency: Use tools like Google Trends, YouTube's own search tools, or specialized SEO tools to analyze the historical search volume and interest for topics in your niche. If there is consistent interest over a long period (years), it's likely that the niche is evergreen.
Future Relevance: Ask yourself, does this topic have future relevance? Evergreen niches often have an inherent longevity to them. Topics like education, health, personal finance, fitness, cooking, and travel tend to be evergreen because they'll always be relevant to people's lives.
Audience Demographics: Consider who your audience is. If your audience is a specific age group that will age out of your content, it might not be an evergreen niche. But if your content is appealing to a broad demographic range, it's more likely to be evergreen.
Inherent Characteristics of the Niche: Some niches are by nature more evergreen than others. For example, niches that rely on timely news or current events may not be as evergreen as niches that focus on timeless topics such as beauty and fashion or travel and lifestyle. 
Competitor Analysis: Look at other channels in your niche. If they have been successful for a long period, it's a good indication the niche is evergreen.
Rate of Change: If the core knowledge or skills in your niche change rapidly, it could be a trend. Evergreen content tends to revolve around knowledge or skills that stay relevant for longer periods.

Choosing an evergreen niche doesn't mean your content has to be static. Even within evergreen niches, trends will come and go. Successful YouTubers find ways to integrate trends into their content strategy to keep things fresh and engaging while maintaining their focus on evergreen topics.
Following these research methods can give you a better understanding of the level of demand and competition in your niche and help you make more informed decisions about the content you create for your YouTube channel.
Remember that balance is key! Passion, authority, high CPM, high affiliate potential and researching demand can help you create a sustainable and successful content strategy. Missing out on either one of these factors can be detrimental to your growth.
For instance, if you create content without passion, keeping only monetization in mind, you may feel disinterested after a while or even experience burnout. Whereas if you focus solely on a topic you’re passionate about, your content might not appeal to a wider audience, limiting your channel’s growth and earning potential. Similarly, if you lack authority in your niche, you won’t be able to create content that adds value, builds trust or stands out. Lack of trust or viewership can affect your earnings. 
Not considering CPM potential and high affiliate potential might lower your earnings. While your channel could see some success, it would make little to no money. Moreover, not finding relevant products to promote on your channel can hinder your ability to generate income through affiliate marketing.
Lastly, insufficient research could lead you to enter niches with little audience interest or too much competition, which can impact your growth as well as earnings. If there is no demand for your topic, you won’t get any views no matter how interesting your content is or how much authority you hold.
